description: Settlement lifecycle rules. IMPORTANT: the RBI (Regulation of Payment Aggregators) Directions, 2025 replaced the rigid T+1 / Tn+1 mandate with commercially negotiated timelines that need only be fair, equitable and transparently disclosed. There is therefore NO regulatory T+N to test against. The settlement SLA is a per-merchant CONTRACT field, and discrepancy class L6 is proven against the merchant's own disclosed timeline, not against a regulation.

source.document: Reserve Bank of India (Regulation of Payment Aggregators) Directions, 2025. Settlement credits to merchants may be effected per the PA-merchant agreement provided terms are fair, equitable and transparently disclosed. Escrow segregation and pre-settlement merchant listing remain mandatory.

default_merchant_sla.notes: Used only when a merchant record does not carry its own contracted SLA. Applied as a fallback, never as a regulatory floor.

lifecycle.explanation: A captured transaction sits in AWAITING_CYCLE until its contracted settlement day passes. Only after unsettled_after_sla_days beyond that date, with no settlement line found across ALL subsequent batches, may it be classified L6. This separation is what prevents a not-yet-due transaction from being filed as an unsettled one.

failed_transaction_tat.source_document: RBI DPSS.CO.PD No.629/02.01.014/2019-20 dated 20 Sep 2019, Harmonisation of Turn Around Time
failed_transaction_tat.notes: Governs auto-reversal timelines for failed transactions. Relevant to discrepancy class L5 (orphan refund): a refund debit without the expected reconciliation credit must be aged against this TAT before being classified as an orphan.

holiday_calendar.notes: Banking days exclude weekends and the three fixed-date national holidays (Republic Day, Independence Day, Gandhi Jayanti). RBI publishes state-wise bank holiday lists under the Negotiable Instruments Act; those vary by state and are not modelled.
assumptions: Only the three fixed-date national holidays are observed; state and moveable holidays are not.
A case whose classification flips on a single holiday assumption must escalate; the two-banking-day grace absorbs a single missed holiday.

reconciliation_invariants.statement: A refund or chargeback transaction is debited from the merchant's settlement exactly once.
reconciliation_invariants.basis: Accounting invariant: a single customer refund creates a single merchant liability. A second debit for the same refund id has no corresponding refund event.

reconciliation_invariants.statement: A successful captured payment settles in exactly one batch within its contracted settlement timeline plus grace.
reconciliation_invariants.basis: RBI (Regulation of Payment Aggregators) Directions, 2025 require settlement per the disclosed PA-merchant agreement; the agreement's settlement_sla_days governs the due date.

reconciliation_invariants.statement: Device rental is debited only for months that start on or after the rental-free period ends and before the device is returned.
reconciliation_invariants.basis: The device subscription record (activation, rental-free period, return with reference) is the contract. A debit outside it has no basis.

reconciliation_invariants.statement: A payment settles on or before its contracted settlement date plus grace.
reconciliation_invariants.basis: RBI (Regulation of Payment Aggregators) Directions, 2025 require settlement per the disclosed agreement. A breach is reported and escalated to settlement operations; it is not a money claim, because no penalty for late settlement is specified in the agreement.
